target_customer: Colleges, universities and schools running alumni and donor fundraising
problem: Traditional university fundraising by phone and mail fails to engage younger alumni; only about 8 percent gave to their college in the prior year per YC.
business_model: B2B SaaS and fundraising platform fees from schools

competitors.name: Kickstarter
competitors.what: General crowdfunding platform that GiveCampus compared itself to, adding a social network and restricting giving to schools

competitors.name: Traditional phone and mail university fundraising
competitors.what: Incumbent approach described by YC as not working

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments and campaign pages with a social layer; mainly integration with school systems and payment compliance.

defensibility.rationale: Relationships and integrations with over 1,500 schools make replacement hard, though crowdfunding pages were copyable early on.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or replaced GiveCampus in sources found; GiveCampus itself acquired Community Funded in June 2023.

market_need_then: YC's post cited that about 90 percent of graduates give to charity but only 8.2 percent gave to their college, and the founders disliked how their own alma mater solicited them.

branding.domain_note: Marketing site is go.givecampus.com on a subdomain; the exact domain history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name with clear meaning for schools, but no evidence of consumer brand pull; growth came from sales to schools.

outcome_analysis: GiveCampus grew slowly and profitably on under 1 million dollars of early money, then took its first institutional capital of 50 million dollars in 2022 and acquired Community Funded in 2023. It now claims over 7 billion dollars raised for more than 1,500 schools.
notes: Company site safety check was rate limited so no fetch. Business Wire page returned 403; the 50M details come from search summaries of WilmerHale and Business Wire. Other sources call the 2022 round growth equity not Series A; label follows WilmerHale. A later 140M growth investment appears only on an undated company blog snippet and is unverified. Search snippets say both founders are Johns Hopkins alumni but that page could not be opened so education is null. Pre-2022 raise was under 1M with no amount stated.
